title.zh-TW: 移除 usage 不誤刪狀態列，讀壞掛鉤檔就停手
title.en: Removing usage preserves your status line, and unreadable hooks stop safely

body.zh-TW: 你曾把自己設定的終端機狀態列（終端機最底下顯示目前狀況的地方）留著，卻在移除 usage 加上的 Codex 狀態列時擔心它一起消失嗎？現在移除動作會逐字核對，只有完全等於 `CODEX_STATUS_LINE` 的那一列才會動；備份檔壞掉或內容型別不對時，設定和備份都原封不動。另一道保護留給掛鉤（特定事件發生時被觸發的小程式）：`~/.codex/hooks.json` 不可讀時，usage 會中止，不再把它當空檔重寫，避免清掉你全部掛鉤，也不會留下半套安裝。像收走租來的衣架，先認準自己的標籤；看不清置物櫃裡的東西，就先不碰。
body.en: If you kept your own terminal status line, removing the Codex line added by usage used to risk taking yours with it. Removal now compares the text exactly and touches only a line equal to `CODEX_STATUS_LINE`; if its backup is corrupt or has the wrong type, both the configuration and backup stay untouched. A second safeguard covers hooks (small programs triggered by particular events): when `~/.codex/hooks.json` cannot be read, usage stops instead of treating it as empty and writing it back. That protects every hook and avoids leaving a half-installed state. It is like collecting rented coat hangers only after checking their labels; if you cannot see inside a locker, you leave it alone.

items.original:
**Removing the Codex status line no longer deletes one that `usage` never installed.** `_unsetup_codex()` only checked whether a `tui.status_line` existed at all, not whether it was ours. Anyone who had configured their own status line and then ran the removal lost it. Worse, a corrupt backup file made the restore path overwrite the config with an empty list and then delete the only backup, losing both at once. Removal now acts only when the status line matches `CODEX_STATUS_LINE` exactly, and an unreadable or wrong-typed backup leaves both the config and the backup untouched.
**A corrupt `~/.codex/hooks.json` is no longer treated as an empty one.** `_load_codex_hooks()` returned `{}` for "file missing" and "file exists but won't parse" alike; terse mode then rebuilt from that empty dict and wrote it back, permanently erasing every Codex hook the user had, with no backup and no message. Codex writing that file while `usage` reads it is enough to trigger this. The unreadable case now aborts before anything is copied or written, so a failed run can no longer leave a half-installed state either.
